experiment.name: Checkout Experiment
experiment.hypothesis: Changing the checkout button color from gray (Control) to bright green (Variant) will make the call-to-action more visually prominent. This will increase the click-through rate by 5% because it reduces visual friction and guides users clearly toward the next step.

verdict.reason: The test has ended and both choices still risk more than your 0.050 pp limit (ship 0.097 pp, keep 0.435 pp).

placebo.text: The rule often picks a winner when nothing differs. In 200 random splits of your control users into two identical groups of 3,021, it named a safer arm 34.5% of the time. Your risk threshold is loose compared with the noise in this metric; a smaller threshold makes the rule more cautious.

label_rule: Secondary metrics are labelled Win when the chance the variant is better is 90% or more, Loss when it is 10% or less, and Neutral in between.
